- Ruling adopted (controller): `readNeonSession` now returns `Promise<{session: VerifiedSession|null; setCookies: string[]}>`. Task 6 must consume this shape and apply returned cookies to the browser response. Cost if wrong: authorization wiring without applying the cookies can miss provider renewal/clearing, so the contract is explicit and tested for renewed and clearing multiple cookies.
- I1 malformed success: the installed SDK converts invalid JSON to `data:null,error:null`, so a normalized-SDK check cannot distinguish invalid JSON from signed-out. The adapter now parses the raw single-hop upstream body itself. Invalid JSON, arrays/non-objects, wrong shapes, and incomplete sessions (missing id/email/expiry) raise `AdminAuthDependencyError` (`dependency_unavailable`, 503). Only JSON `null` and `{session:null,user:null}` are supported signed-out; a well-formed expired session is null. Regressions added for 200 invalid JSON, wrong shape, incomplete session, mixed null shapes, oversized response, and both signed-out shapes.
- I2 credential exposure: the toolkit's response allowlist forwards `set-auth-token`/`set-auth-jwt` and returns provider token bodies. The adapter now constructs the browser response itself, forwards no provider credential headers, and normalizes successful browser responses to `{ok,user:{id,email,emailVerified,name}|null,session:{expiresAt}|null}` with no bearer/session/refresh/JWT fields. Regressions assert a realistic sign-in body/headers and a `get-session` proxy response expose no token.
- I3 redirect control: `handleAuthProxyRequest`/`createAuthServer` fetch without `redirect:"manual"` and strip `Location`, so post-fetch rewriting was too late. The proxy is now a narrow controlled single-hop `fetch` with `redirect:"manual"`, no retry/hop, forwarded caller `Authorization`/`Host`/`Referer` removed, trusted `Origin` set, and only a validated same-origin `/admin` `Location` (relative or absolute public-origin) or the secure default emitted. Regression: intercepted `verify-email` 302 with a malicious target and two cookies; the target is never fetched (counter 0) and cookies are retained.
- I4 cookie updates: the previous session context `setCookie` was a no-op. The new read contract accumulates up to 8 sanitized Neon-prefixed provider cookies (renewal/clearing/rotation) and returns them; the same sanitizer runs on the proxy path. Regressions cover renewed plus clearing multiple cookies on a valid read and a clearing cookie on a rejected read.
- SDK behavior recorded: the installed `@neondatabase/auth@0.6.0-beta` server transport follows redirects by default, allowlists `set-auth-token`/`set-auth-jwt`, and maps invalid JSON to `data:null,error:null`. The adapter still pins/imports the SDK for its stable cookie primitives (`extractNeonAuthCookies`, `parseSetCookies`, `serializeSetCookie`, `NEON_AUTH_COOKIE_PREFIX`) and dynamically loads it only on explicit neon-mode auth requests so default access-mode startup is unaffected.
